question: The Chinese market is an essential and non-substitutable market for EU spirits. It is the world’s largest market for spirits overall, in terms of both value and volume, and the second largest export market for EU spirits after the United States, with exports worth EUR 875 million in 2022 (88 % of which were wine-based spirits).

On 5 January 2024, China announced the opening of an anti-dumping investigation into European wines and grape marc spirits imported into the country. This measure echoes the anti-subsidy investigation launched by the Commission against Chinese electric vehicles.

With the EU-US trade dispute over Airbus/Boeing still unresolved, both of the two main export markets for grape-based spirits are experiencing a certain slowdown at the moment. In view of this situation: 1.
What steps does the Commission intend to take in order to prevent the introduction of Chinese tariffs on EU spirit imports?
Given the need for a constructive dialogue, is the Commission planning to restart the EU-China Working Group on Alcoholic Beverages, as announced last September?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.4.2024) The Commission is fully aware of the importance of this case for the EU spirit drinks industry. The Commission is following the investigation very closely and is determined to support the EU industry. Commission services have been active in defending the interests of the EU producers concerned since the beginning of the investigation.

A first submission has been sent to the Chinese authorities at the beginning of February 2024, another one – in March 2024, and further interventions in support of the EU industry will follow as appropriate, in the subsequent stages of the procedure. The Commission is also intervening at the political level.

Nevertheless, the full cooperation by the EU exporting producers with the Chinese authorities throughout the investigation is of critical importance. While some companies may find such cooperation burdensome and costly, such cooperation is indispensable. The EU and China agreed, in their High-level Economic Dialogue of September 2023 to restart the EU-China Working Group on Alcoholic Beverages1.

This Working Group should provide a regulatory dialogue forum to address issues of interest to the EU and China alcoholic beverages sectors. The Commission is currently discussing with the relevant Chinese administrations in view of holding a meeting of this working group in the coming weeks.
